sentences.text: In Argentina, 40% of the vote can make you president.
Who can vote? Every citizen from 16, and it's a must from 18 to 70. Citizens abroad can vote too.
Since 2025, there's one paper ballot: a row per race, a column per party. Tick one box per row, fold it, and drop it in.
Deputies are shared out by vote share in each province, above a 3% line. Half are elected every two years.
That's the 257-member Chamber of Deputies, which makes the laws. The Senate must pass them too: three per province, one for the runner-up.
The president runs the government. 45% wins in round one, or 40% with a ten-point lead. If not, there's a run-off.
In 2023, Javier Milei won the run-off with 55.7%. In 2025, his party won the midterms, but still has no majority.
So, should 16-year-olds help choose who runs a country?
